item.title: Critique + Request for expansion
item.content:encoded:
Alright, so you may or may not recognize me from various (video game) modding communities, so it's fitting my first forum comment is on something that is more-or-less "video game glitch: the SCP - exploration log."

First off, love the idea, love the logs. I think the main SCP itself could be tweaked a bit to incorporate more of the "this is junk data" theme in it without giving the whole game away, and would benefit greatly from it. As it was I felt like I was reading an SCP on Diagon Alley or Danny the Street until I got to the logs. Ambiguity isn't a bad thing in that regard though, more of a personal preference.

+ show block
– hide block

Second, I'm going to echo what a lot of other commenters have said about the use of "[REDACTED]", in that I think most of the uses add nothing to the narrative as it is. Most are too ambiguous to really do much other than serve as narrative speed bumps that slow the reader down. A little modification could make them a bit more thematically appropriate without reducing the effective blanking of information. For example (not to pick on this section), you could say something like:

Food was found to be fresh and edible, though unusually high in compounds known to cause [REDACTED], consistent with the effects of SCP-████.

That implies a reason for the redaction without actually explaining anything, and makes it a lot less jarring.

Third, I think ambiguity in general is the largest thing that undermines this log. Aside from the previously identified section about the plants with "heavy levels of mutation" that gives no specifics as to what kind of mutation, what stands out to me the most are the accounts of the recovered computer hardware. The log indicates that the hardware itself is to blame for the errors, but fails to elaborate on what or why. I could see that as being more relevant for an addendum or Recovered Materials log, but it should at least be mentioned in the Survey Log that further examination is taking place; I CANNOT imagine the Foundation not putting that hardware under the microscope (literally) to figure out what exactly is wrong with it. As for what they find, terms like "non-Euclidean geometries" spring to mind.

Fourth, that previous thought leads me to a recommendation: expand this please. More Survey Logs, maybe a Recovered Materials Log, and just a little more detail into the "junk data" nature of this little slice of weird reality. Just a little more filling in would improve this and its parent skip a lot. Hell, this seems like the perfect sort of place for some section of the Foundation to try and establish some kind of storage facility, testing area, emergency bunker, or who knows what else. The loss of a handful of agents rules out more "safe" uses, but the Foundation has set up research facilities in far less hospitable conditions with far more additional loss. They certainly don't abandon potential storage areas with built-in limited access before they are utterly sure they can't counteract the negative effects of said areas.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

In other words, throw more Agents and D-class into the grinder and write about the results!

item.content:encoded:
My thoughts exactly. How I see it is the infinite falling effect happens when the explorer leaves the (procedurally generated, I think) semi-random map area and "falls off", becoming only able to see the skybox.
I've seen this effect countless times in Fallout 3 and New Vegas, both through glitches and no clipping cheating. Sometimes the whole map even becomes invisible unless you can re-enter its bounds which seems to be the case here.
I can see how this skip can be confusing without a good deal of experience playing 3D games.

item.content:encoded:
Just wanted to say that I disagree with most of these points, at least those about "REDACTED" usage.

I used my imagination, and enjoyed it a lot. Don't know what more to say about that..

That being said, I agree on a few things. The gangster against the wall is one. I imagine he was on the ground leaning against the wall, but the original quote is too ambiguous here. At first it sounds like he's standing up while leaning against the wall as a skeleton, which makes no sense neither technically nor "lore"-logically..

aged 9, 5, and 8 months

Sentence needs restructuring indeed.

Now to quote howell2010, who I replied to:

Only 7 minutes? Pansies.

I don't get it. What is your logic here? Keep falling (and bouncing) forever OR waiting for yourself to get smashed into pulp, given solid ground eventually appeared? Also, how is logical reasoning related to bravery "bravery" ?

The slacks: A bit annoyed by the nitpicking but I also think you're right. A better sentence would be "(…) pair of black slacks as the only discernable clothing(…)"

Anyways, enjoyed the read. An interesting world for sure, it in some way remind me of a computer generated world, with world "edges" (which makes you potentially fall forever, original map disappearing further into the distance) and backdrops that never get closer.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This, and moose's thing. Very much this.

Does anyone remember the red stone disc that sticks to mirrors and allows passage to another world where everything's gotten severely fucky depending on the color an individual person makes the disc turn? That scip's experiment log had a significant creep factor. (And yes, I know others have made this comparison, but it's a no-brainer comparison, really it is.) What disappoints me so much about this test log is that it feels like it could be just as much - possibly even the same basic idea and length and of equal quality, but significantly different enough in details to make it unique - except it feels like the author sort of stopped halfway through and never finished it. There are few things more tragic than a story left only half-told and never finished.

When the (+100-ed) article itself was lackluster but had a link to a test log, I thought to myself "Oh, it's one of those articles where you have to read the test log to understand why it's so freaky." Then I thought, "Haha, watch the test log be just as lackluster." I have never been less happy to be right about something, ever. This test log here is a demo, a teaser - a lot of (really good!) buildup to a climax that never comes. There is so much that can and should be done with this, but it cops out just when it's getting really interesting.

If you're trying to make a scip that relies on its test log, but I still have to read the discussion pages to get what's going on even after reading that test log, the article can't really be called complete. Now that I have read the discussion pages and get what's going on…I'm not sure if I'm less annoyed or more annoyed by the lack of substance in the articles. It's real-life level zero, and that's cool. It presents an "edge of the world" for people to fall off of, and that's cool. There are glitchy, presumably hostile entities we can't hunt down roaming around in there, and that's really cool. Imagine if you could get to level zero in a game, and not only is it a glitchy world, but there are new (or I guess, leftover-bit-glitchy) enemies that don't appear in the real game that can appear and kill you but you don't really get to see them and don't know what they do or anything - that would be beyond awesome. And what would gamers do if someone discovered such a thing in a game and went on the internet and told everyone about it? Pretty much what the Foundation ought to do upon discovering the place in real life: Brave all the dangers and face all the fears to try and figure out exactly what the actual hell is going on. They'd race to be the first to get screenshots of the monsters, they'd walk right to the edge to try and figure out exactly where the world ends to the nearest centimeter, they'd have competitions to see who can survive the nighttime in the level the longest or who can survive the most nighttimes, and they'd try to record as much of it to post on the internet as possible to prove their prowess. The Foundation should be doing pretty much the IRL equivalent of that with this thing. It's much easier to Secure, Contain, and Protect a thing the more you understand it, and the Foundation tries to make sense of all the nonsensical things it exists to contain for that very reason.

And why nighttime? And how did the Foundation figure out not to be in there at nighttime? And why won't people talk about what happens at night? That gets into Howell's comments, which I've already thirded, but seriously, so much could be done here!

With over +100 on the log as well as the main article, I feel cheated. I may be only one person, but even as much as I love the idea behind this scip and the test log, and as much as I love to upvote things, I will still withhold my upvote on both pages because they haven't been fully fleshed out. If that isn't worth squat, so be it.

item.content:encoded:
This is one of the more disturbing things I have read on this site.

This kind of idea is right up my alley (awful pun intended). It reminds me of the "Minus World" in Super Mario Bros… i.e. a place that was not actually designed, and that no one was ever supposed to go… a place that just popped into existence by itself, via corruption of existing data.

I always found the Mario "Minus World" mildly disturbing for that very reason (it's a playable video game level, yet no one actually designed it)… I find this file disturbing for the same reason, only this one is much, much worse, for obvious reasons.

Well done. Enthusiastic +1 (for both the original file and the survey reports)

Edit: one very minor complaint - I agree with everyone else about the "psuedopods" - it just doesn't fit the feel of the rest of the file.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm not attempting to necro this, I just want to answer this question because while reading, that term really bugged me.

Memory Dump would be acceptable for my enjoyment.

and "Divide by zero" errors is too colloquial for me as well.

Certain redactions are really annoying to me as well, and indicate laziness(to me)

Food was found to be fresh and edible, though unusually high in compounds known to cause [REDACTED].

It is better reading if the compound was named, or left redacted but had at least one symptom mentioned. Otherwise it reads like "Food was found to be fresh and edible, though unusually high in compounds known to cause cats to gather and re-enact the Battle of Gettysburg."

The final photo showed a [REDACTED].

a view so beautiful that we couldn't mention it for fear of creating a cognitohazard?

Survivor was highly confused about what had happened during the time contact was lost and the S&R team located him, only repeating that [REDACTED]

Only repeating "Popeye's chicken is the shit!"
Also would be better sentence structure to say "highly confused about what had happened between the time contact was lost and when the S&R team located him"

Other things that bother me are…

Plant samples were found to exhibit an abnormally high amount of mutation.

What kind of mutation?

█████████, several thousand kilometers away.

That one I just find strange. Several thousand km away from where?

Canvassing of the area proved unable to locate the owner/s of the vehicle prior to abandoning SCP-1165 for the day due to impending twilight.

Am I missing where it said to not be in 1165 after dark? Cause some of the later distances surely would take more time that possible to travel there and back before dark.

leaning against a wall in an alleyway, the skeletal remains of an adult male

He was standing up?

The remains of ██████'s wife and children, aged 9, 5, and 8 months,

His wife is 9 years old? o.0 and has 2 kids aged 5 and 8 months? o.0 So she had a child when she was 4? o.0
Or, did he have 3 kids and you just didn't mention his wife's age? And how would the foundation know exactly how old the children were if the father was just a skeleton?

After 7 minutes without reaching the ground, pilot and support team committed suicide by gunshot.

Only 7 minutes? Pansies.

The corpse was nude except for a pair of black slacks.

First, it would probably sound more clinical to say body. At least right here.
Second… The body was nude except for being clothed? I think you should find a way to say it without using the word nude, because it isn't nude it is clothed.

That's all the major things.

The rest is just the tone. It doesn't feel clinical enough, or like a debrief.

I love the idea of this SCP. These are my favorite kind of SCPs, but this one isn't done well…
I'm holding my upvote until the tone is fixed.

I won't downvote though, cause I see potential.

I really like this. Lots of good detail.

That helicopter thing, man. Fuck. And Stevenson. Great stuff.

One nitpick:

The final photo showed a [REDACTED].

Pretty bullshit redaction - it doesn't imply anything except that 'there is something interesting here which the author decided to keep from me for no reason, OR the author was lazy and wanted to add cheap mystery factor here'.

Besides that… I don't like where it ends. I really want more. I also think that:

Further surveys of an area within 1 sq. km. of the warehouse are preemptively denied.

…is also bullshit. Since when does the Foundation not want to figure out more shit. Since when I ask you.

Anyway, besides those issues, I think this is pretty damn great.

item.content:encoded:
I've actually never played any of the Silent Hill games.

My original concept for the creature, in line with the junk data aspect I mentioned earlier, was for it to be a pixellated blob and have bits and pieces sticking out all over the place. I couldn't find a way to describe that that sounded dry and clinical enough, so I went with pseudopods instead, because everyone loves pseudopods. The fact that the photographs came out corrupted, and the radio static noise (which isn't necessarily coming from the same kind of creature as the corpse was), are leftover elements from that.
